key_insight: AutoGaze is a lightweight autoregressive module that 'looks' only at informative spatiotemporal patches before a ViT or MLLM, removing redundant pixels so long, high-resolution videos can be processed much more efficiently without retraining large vision backbones.
problem_solved: Current MLLMs and ViTs waste compute and memory by processing every pixel of long, high-resolution videos equally, struggling with spatiotemporal redundancy and scaling to long clips.
method: Insert a small AutoGaze module that autoregressively selects a minimal set of spatiotemporal patches (multi-scale) to keep for downstream vision/MLLM processing.
Train selection with next-token prediction augmented by reinforcement learning to balance information retention and sparsity.
Feed only the retained patches to an off-the-shelf ViT or MLLM, enabling plug-and-play compute and memory savings while preserving video understanding performance.
impact: Makes multimodal LLMs and vision transformers practical for long, high-resolution video tasks by significantly reducing inference/training compute and memory, lowering latency and cost while retaining accuracy.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: video frames → AutoGaze (gaze arrows) → retained patches → ViT/MLLM → output
Before/after frame: full-frame attention vs. sparse retained patches highlighted
Compute vs. sequence length chart: baseline (full) vs AutoGaze showing lower FLOPs/memory at scale
Gaze trajectory heatmap or temporal strip showing where AutoGaze attends across time
paper_title: Attend Before Attention: Efficient and Scalable Video Understanding via Autoregressive Gazing
paper_authors: Baifeng Shi, Stephanie Fu, Long Lian, Hanrong Ye, David Eigen
